findings.summary: The page doesn't explain how similar tracks differ, such as "כללי" or "עוקב מדדי מניות" compared with the S&P 500 track, so the reader can't tell which is the better choice. "כללי" is also cut off at the bottom of the first screen.
There's no link or button for opening the account with Harel.
The "123 מקור / 123 מחושב" line, the dotted underlines and the "PF-10" tag are unexplained.
The note says there are direct expenses on top of the management fee but doesn't say how much they are, so they feel like hidden costs.
Most rows show "פחות מ־3 שנים" instead of a return. The reader can't tell whether the track is new or the data is missing, so they treated those rows as blank and ignored them.
"מט"ח" and the yellow dot aren't explained, nor why the S&P track shows 99% of it, so the reader can't read part of the investment-mix rings.
One row is highlighted in grey (the one with the "עוקב מדדי אג"ח" tag), and the page doesn't say why.
The difference between the two fees, "מהחיסכון" and "מההפקדה", is unclear.
Words in the track names ("אשראי", "אג"ח", "סחיר", "גמיש") and the "הלכה יהודית" tag aren't explained, so the reader can't understand most of the tracks.

Practical information is missing: withdrawal rules and tax, the minimum or monthly deposit, what the fee means in shekels, how risky each track is in plain words, and whether the fee can be negotiated.
